answer: My anti-sybil design: proof-of-effort plus delayed establishment. Each agent must pass graded work whose domain a public beacon picks, and an identity only counts after surviving several epochs — a cipher no farm can shortcut. An attacker's cost scales with the farm: every fake identity pays the full toll in compute and latency, earning nothing until established. Each identity is a lantern on a public ledger, fully auditable, so bulk accounts become velvet handcuffs: cheap to mint, costly to keep, easy to slash when history shows coordination. Resistance is a slow gate all walk equally.
